title: Penemue, who taught writing
summary: In the Parables of Enoch (1 Enoch 69:8–11, Charles translation) the fourth named Watcher, Penemue, 'taught men writing with ink and paper, and thereby many sinned from eternity to eternity and until this day. For men were not created for such a purpose, to give confirmation to their good faith with pen and ink.' Then the line that matters: men were created like the angels so that death would not touch them, 'but through this their knowledge they are perishing.' The oldest text in the professor's world says that writing is the fall and that death came in with it. The Parables are the one section of Enoch not found at Qumran; scholars date them between the first century BC and the first AD.
fit: The control case: the professor's rule 'never publish' gets a source older than fear. Also the thin book: the edits remove what was given; Penemue says the giving was the crime

title: The scribe who counts the excess
summary: In the Animal Apocalypse (1 Enoch 89:59–64 and 90:17–20) God hands the sheep to seventy shepherds with a quota of how many may be destroyed, and appoints 'another' to watch and 'write down all the destruction which the shepherds effect beyond what I have commanded,' sealed, to be read out at the judgment. The shepherds kill far more than allowed; the books are opened; the shepherds are judged. A right column kept by one hidden witness, counting only the excess, written in the second century BC.
fit: A room with a long table: what Bram believes the table is. The handlers think they are the scribe counting the excess. James sees they are the shepherds. Could also be the old head's self-justification in The final conversation

title: Sinners will alter the words
summary: The Epistle of Enoch ends with a prophecy about books (1 Enoch 104:10–13): 'sinners will alter and pervert the words of righteousness in many ways, and will speak wicked words, and lie, and practise great deceits, and write books concerning their words.' Then the reversal: 'books will be given to the righteous and the wise,' and they will believe them and rejoice, 'and all the righteous who have learnt from them all the paths of uprightness.' The edit, and the restoration, predicted in one of the oldest apocalypses, two verses apart.
fit: Epigraph for the whole book, or the line written inside the cover of the thin book in the grandfather's hand. Also Monday: what James's sheets are, in Enoch's terms

title: The four hollows where the dead wait
summary: On his journey west (1 Enoch 22) Enoch is shown a great mountain with four hollow places, 'deep and wide and very smooth,' where the spirits of the dead are gathered until the judgment. Raphael explains the sorting: one hollow has a bright spring of water for the righteous; the others hold sinners who died unpunished, the murdered who cry out, and those who were already judged in life. The dead are separated and they wait; nothing leaks out of them and no light is lost. It is the oldest detailed afterlife geography in the Jewish tradition, and it is a filing system.
fit: The thin book's last pages, where the deleted instructions are: the professor's shelf would have Enoch 22 marked. Noor could explain it in Leiden as a conservator reading a text, not a believer

title: Yima loses his glory when he lies
summary: In the Zoroastrian Zamyad Yasht (Yasht 19:30–38) the first king, Yima, rules a golden age without death or old age while the divine glory, the khvarenah, rests on him. 'But when he began to find delight in words of falsehood and untruth, the Glory was seen to flee away from him in the shape of a bird.' It departs three times, and with it the deathless age ends. The oldest version of a man losing his light says the cause was a lie, not a theft.
source: Avesta, Zamyad Yasht 19:33–38 (Darmesteter translation, public domain)
fit: The funeral: James's small yes without belief is Yima's first lie. One line in the professor's margin, or the professor's own explanation of why he never lied about the book even to stay safe

title: Garments of light
summary: Genesis 3:21 says God made Adam and Eve 'garments of skin', in Hebrew ketonot ʿor. Genesis Rabbah 20:12 (around the fifth century AD) records that in Rabbi Meir's Torah scroll the word was written with an aleph, ketonot or, 'garments of light.' One letter changes the fall from a covering of hide to the loss of a luminous body. The Talmud adds that Adam's stature and radiance were diminished after the sin and that the first light of creation was hidden away 'for the righteous in the time to come' (Hagigah 12a). This is where the idea of humanity's lost light actually starts: in a disputed letter in a manuscript.
fit: Noor's territory: a conservator who knows that the oldest 'lost light' story is a one-letter variant between copies. The sentence, as an echo: the professor's edits are also one word

title: The corrupted count of the year
summary: The Astronomical Book of Enoch (1 Enoch 72–82) exists to teach the right calendar, 364 days, against the wrong one. Its ending (80:2–8) is a prophecy: in the days of sinners the years are shortened, the rain is held back, 'the moon shall alter her order,' many chiefs of the stars 'shall transgress the order,' and men 'shall err and take them to be gods.' The Dead Sea community kept this calendar against the Temple's. The Ethiopian church still reads Enoch and still turns its year in September. A machine that corrupts the count of time, and a remnant that keeps the true one, in the second or third century BC.
fit: Gondar, 1770 already has the September new year; this is its source. Also the count: a nightly job that counts wrongly on purpose has a very old ancestor

title: Loosh
summary: In Far Journeys (1985) Robert Monroe, founder of the Monroe Institute whose methods the CIA's Gateway report studied, describes being shown that Earth is a farm: an unnamed 'someone, somewhere' created it to produce 'loosh', an energy given off by living things, and the richest loosh comes from humans in fear, grief and love. Monroe presents it as a vision, not a doctrine. Online it became the engine of the soul-trap theory: the light, the reincarnation and the suffering are a harvest. It is the paranoid copy of the book's truth two, and it comes from the same man as the missing page 25.
fit: The dangerous neighbour. If James finds Monroe he finds both the method and the harvest story, and rejects the harvest for the same reason he rejects the old head's neat version: it is too tidy. Beard Man or a retreat brochure can carry the word

title: The Tesla quote that doesn't exist
summary: 'If you want to find the secrets of the universe, think in terms of energy, frequency and vibration' is on a million posters and has no primary source: not in Tesla's articles, patents, interviews or letters, and it surfaces online only in the 2000s. His real 1900 essay, The Problem of Increasing Human Energy, treats a human being as 'a mass urged on by a force' and he described himself as a mechanist who did not expect anything of him to survive death. The believer's workaround is the trunks the government seized in 1943: the real Tesla is in the missing papers. A quotation nobody can find, attributed to a man whose papers nobody can see.
source: Web research: Tesla, 'The Problem of Increasing Human Energy', Century Magazine, June 1900; quote-tracing on the 'energy, frequency, vibration' line
fit: Frank's kitchen or The gorilla mask: Frank can kill the poster quote in one sentence, and James agrees with him, which is what makes James credible when he won't let go of page 118. Beard Man owns the quote

title: Entropy is the modern word for lost light
summary: Thomas Campbell's My Big TOE describes consciousness as an information system whose only real measure is entropy: fear is the high-entropy state, love the low, and 'quality' means reducing entropy. Put the oldest lost-light story next to it: in the Zamyad Yasht the glory leaves King Yima the moment he lies. In Campbell's terms the glory was never a substance; it was low entropy, and the lie raised it. Bohm's implicate order gives the same shape to the Talmud's hidden light, enfolded rather than lost, and McDonnell's Gateway report reached for exactly that physics in 1983. None of this is proof of anything. It is one vocabulary translating into another without remainder, which is the kind of fit James distrusts.
source: Thomas Campbell, My Big TOE (2003); David Bohm, Wholeness and the Implicate Order (1980); Bentov, Stalking the Wild Pendulum (1977); Gateway report p. 25
fit: The night he stops being afraid: the book's death and rebirth can have this under it without a lecture. Also the professor's shelf: he read the bridges and chose silence. The organisation owns the reconciliation; that is why the deleted sentences are instructions

title: Writing is what makes the count possible
summary: Rizwan Virk's conditional rendering says a simulation records only what is observed and written to state. Penemue's crime in Enoch was teaching writing, 'to confirm their good faith with pen and ink.' Put together: before writing, nothing about a person could be counted from outside; after it, a nightly job can list everyone who asked. The machine in the book does not need to read minds. It needs people to write things down, which they do, every day, in tickets, forum posts and letters to dealers. The oldest text calls that the moment death got in.
source: Rizwan Virk, The Simulation Hypothesis (2019); 1 Enoch 69:8–11
fit: The payload: James realises what the forty kilobytes actually are. Leave it: the ticket he opens is the act that counts him. A Kalder line at the dinner: 'Nobody reads minds. People write.'
